subject: Agriculture
title: No-Till Farming
description: A quick, practical guide to No-Till Farming.

hook.text: For centuries, plowing was farming's first step. A growing movement says: stop plowing entirely.

buildup.text: No-till farming plants seeds directly into undisturbed soil using special drills that cut through residue.

discovery.text: Skipping the plow preserves soil structure, protects earthworms, and keeps carbon locked underground.

twist.text: Without tillage, weeds are harder to control. Many no-till farmers rely more heavily on herbicides.

climax.text: No-till is spreading fast—now used on over 150 million hectares worldwide, especially in the Americas.

punchline.text: The best thing some farmers do is nothing—no plow, no till.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of no-till farming for soil?
options: It preserves soil structure, protects organisms, and stores carbon
